children: Updating on trading, the chain said like-for-like sales in the 13 weeks to 31 October had fallen 2.6% to £2.9bn, or by 1.1% on an organic basis.

Within that, conditions improved in North America compared to the second quarter, and organic growth ticked up 0.5%. But in Europe, like-for-like sales fell 2.7%, impacted by unseasonably warm weather at the start of autumn and civil unrest in France.

As a result, JD Sports narrowed its full-year guidance. It now expects pre-tax profits before adjusting items to come in between £700m and £750m, from previous expectations for between £700m and £800m. Guidance for free cash flow was left unchanged, for between £460m and £520m.

Regis Schultz, chief executive, said trading had been in line with expectations, with like-for-like sales improving on the second-quarter, when they fell 3.1%. He continued: "North America improved on the second quarter, our sporting goods and outdoor businesses performed well and sales trends in apparel and accessories were resilient.
"Our multi-brand, multi-category model keeps us agile and quick to respond to changing customer trends and demands.
"We remain disciplined on costs, capital and inventory, with further supply chain efficiencies coming through as automation at our Heerlen distribution centre in Europe progresses."
